title: Shape effects on the Shafranov shift of Solov'ev equilibria with prescribed boundaries
abstract: The Shafranov shift, the outward displacement of the magnetic axis of a toroidal plasma, is known analytically for circular and elliptical cross-sections, whereas its dependence on shape in strongly shaped plasmas has not been studied systematically. Here the shift is analyzed for a wide range of prescribed boundaries, at fixed profiles or poloidal beta, using exact Solov'ev solutions of the Grad--Shafranov equation with the boundary imposed in a least-squares sense. For shaped boundaries the shift depends on the point from which it is measured, usually the geometric center, the midpoint of the radial extent of the boundary. Therefore, a straight-cylinder equilibrium with the same plasma shape is introduced as the zero-shift reference state, and the shift is measured from its magnetic axis. With this reference, some known features of the shift measured from the geometric center turn out to be effects of the reference point, whose error depends only on the boundary and can also make the shift negative. Three boundary parametrizations are used to analyze positive and negative triangularity, squareness from square to concave shapes, and non-convex star polygons of arbitrary symmetry order. At fixed poloidal beta the shift depends only weakly on triangularity: the larger shift of negative than of positive triangularity plasmas obtained with the geometric center is an effect of the reference point and nearly disappears with the cylindrical reference. Negative squareness and concavity, instead, reduce the shift itself: for concave plasma cross-sections it is almost half that of elliptical and D-shaped ones.
